title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JIMMY'S QUILT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Jimmy Delgado, a fifty-six-year-old railroad conductor from Pocatello, Idaho.
Big hands. Loud voice. Thirty years of freight trains.
And one day, he made a promise he could not sew his way out of.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PROMISE
segments.quote: The beautiful thing about learning is nobody can take it away from you.
segments.author: B. B. King
lines: His daughter Rosa was having her first baby in the spring.
Jimmy said, I'll make the baby a quilt. Then he heard what he said.
At the library, a sign read Thursday Night Stitchers. Under it, a line from the blues legend B. B. King:
The beautiful thing about learning is nobody can take it away from you.
Jimmy sat down with six ladies. The youngest was seventy.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: SLOW DOWN
segments.quote: Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
segments.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
lines: He ran the sewing machine like a freight train. The seams came out like a mountain road.
Dot, who was eighty-one, put her hand on his and quoted the French writer Rousseau:
Patience is bitter, but its fruit is sweet.
So Jimmy slowed down. One square. Then another. Straight, almost.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: SORE THUMBS
segments.quote: Life grants nothing to us mortals without hard work.
segments.author: Horace
lines: Every night after his shift, he sewed at the kitchen table.
His thumbs were full of pin holes. He wanted to buy a quilt online.
Then he saw Dot's note pinned to his fabric, from the Roman poet Horace:
Life grants nothing to us mortals without hard work.
He taped up his thumbs and sewed until midnight.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BAD CUT
segments.quote: There is no failure except in no longer trying.
segments.author: Elbert Hubbard
lines: Two weeks before the baby shower, he cut the big middle piece six inches too short.
He drove off to buy a quilt. On the radio, a host read a line from the writer Elbert Hubbard:
There is no failure except in no longer trying.
He drove home and filled the gap with a stripe from his old railroad vest. Best part of the quilt.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: DOT'S QUILT
segments.quote: Envy is the art of counting the other fellow's blessings instead of your own.
segments.author: Harold Coffin
lines: At the last Thursday, Dot showed her quilt. Perfect little stars. Jimmy's looked like it lost a fight.
He went quiet. Dot laughed and quoted the newspaper writer Harold Coffin:
Envy is the art of counting the other fellow's blessings instead of your own.
So he counted his. A railroad stripe. Pin holes. Twelve weeks of Thursdays. That quilt was his.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SHOWER
segments.quote: The manner of giving is worth more than the gift.
segments.author: Pierre Corneille
lines: At the shower, Jimmy almost hid his box.
Rosa opened it, saw the crooked stars and the railroad stripe, and started crying.
Her mom whispered a line from the French playwright Corneille:
The manner of giving is worth more than the gift.
Rosa said, Dad, it's perfect. It was not. It was better.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Learn. Slow down. Work hard. Keep trying. Count your own blessings. Give from the heart.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Learn something new. Slow down. Work hard. Keep trying. Count your own blessings. Give from the heart.
I sewed a button once. My thumb is still attached to that sweater.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
